title: Dilmun settlement on Failaka
description: A settlement on Failaka grew into a station of Dilmun, the Gulf trading civilisation centred on Bahrain.

title: Al Sabah rule begins
description: Sabah I was chosen by the leading families to settle disputes, beginning the Al Sabah dynasty that still rules.

title: Mubarak seizes power
description: Mubarak took the sheikhdom after his half-brother was killed, and his twenty-year reign brought Kuwait closer to Britain.

title: Secret agreement with Britain
description: Mubarak promised Britain not to deal with any other power, making Kuwait a protectorate in all but name against Ottoman pressure.

title: Battle of Jahra
description: Kuwaitis held the Red Fort of Jahra against a much larger Ikhwan force from Nejd until a British warning brought the siege to an end.

title: Uqair Protocol fixes the borders
description: Percy Cox drew the frontiers between Kuwait, Najd and Iraq, costing Kuwait two-thirds of the territory it had claimed.

title: Saudi blockade
description: Ibn Saud kept a tight economic blockade on Kuwait after failing to draw it into his expanding state, deepening the town's poverty.

title: Oil concession signed
description: The sheikh granted a 75-year concession to the Anglo-American group that became the Kuwait Oil Company.

title: Oil discovered at Burgan
description: Drillers struck oil at Burgan, soon found to be one of the largest fields in the world, just as the pearl trade collapsed in the depression.

title: First oil export
description: Sheikh Ahmad turned a silver wheel to send off the first tanker of Kuwaiti crude, opening the country's oil age.

title: Independence
description: Kuwait and Britain ended the 1899 agreement by treaty exchange, and days later British troops returned to deter an Iraqi claim.

title: Constitution promulgated
description: The emir issued a constitution with an elected National Assembly, suspended twice in later decades.

title: Samita border skirmish
description: Iraqi troops attacked a Kuwaiti border post and held it for weeks before withdrawing under Saudi and Soviet pressure.

title: Oil industry fully nationalised
description: The state took over the remaining foreign share of the Kuwait Oil Company, completing its control of the country's only major industry.

title: December bombings
description: Six bombs hit targets including the American and French embassies, attacks linked to Iran-backed militants during the Iran–Iraq War.

title: Attempt on the emir's life
description: A suicide bomber attacked the motorcade of Emir Jaber, who survived with light wounds.

title: Women gain political rights
description: The National Assembly voted to let women vote and stand for parliament, and four women won seats in 2009.

title: Al-Sadeq mosque bombing
description: A suicide bomber killed twenty-seven worshippers at a Shia mosque, the deadliest attack in the country's history.
